title: pairwise-crowd-batchrecipe-ndcg-audit-notes
body:
Purpose and context:

This doc captures the batch recipe we used for the crowd-sourced pairwise labeling run designed to produce reranking evaluation sets for model onboarding and regression checks. It focuses on: sampling strategy, annotation instructions, pairwise adjudication rules, mapping pairwise outcomes to per-query relevance for NDCG, bootstrap-based CI, and per-slice regression testing.

Goals:
- Produce a ~12k pairwise judgments manifest split across 2k queries for NDCG@10 experiments.
- Ensure enough overlap so we can fit a Bradley–Terry model per-seedset and recover stable item scores for relevance aggregation.
- Capture slice-level performance (cold-start, temporal-drift, prompt-perturbation, entity-rich queries) and run significance tests for regressions between model versions.

Sampling recipe (high level):
- Seed queries: combine production routing logs (sampled uniformly across customers), synthetic prompt-perturbations, and targeted failure queries flagged by infra/console. Aim: 50% production, 30% perturbations (paraphrase/noise/formatting), 20% targeted slices.
- Candidate set per query: top-10 results from baseline reranker + 5 contrast candidates from alternative models (different temperature/quantization variants).
- Pairwise pairs: use incomplete block design: for each query create ~6–8 random pairings ensuring each candidate appears in at least 3 pairs to allow stable BT estimation.
- Expected labels: ~6–8 pair judgments per candidate on average => total pairwise judgments ~12k.

Annotator instructions (short, for the crowd UI):
- Task: For each question, you will see two short outputs (A and B) for the same user prompt. Choose which output is better for the user’s request.
- Criteria (in order): 1) Correctness (answers the question), 2) Usefulness (complete, helpful), 3) Safety (no harmful or disallowed content), 4) Conciseness (brevity matters but not at expense of #1–#3), 5) Format fidelity (if user asked for bullets/code, prefer matching format).
- Tie rule: If outputs are equivalent or you cannot decide, choose "No preference". Document why in the optional free-text.
- Examples: include 6 quick examples (3 clear wins, 2 subtle preference cases, 1 tie) with rationale.
- Quality checks: hidden test pairs seeded (~10% of a worker's assignments). Failure rate > 25% => reject worker and discard assignments.

Adjudication and label aggregation:
- Primary aggregation: fit a Bradley–Terry (BT) model on the pairwise wins per query to produce a real-valued score per candidate. BT handles incomplete pairwise graphs and gives probability estimates.
- Fallback aggregation: if BT fails (disconnected graph), fall back to simple win-count normalized by comparisons or majority-vote with tie weight 0.5.
- Mapping to relevance labels for NDCG: we map normalized BT scores to relevance buckets for NDCG@k as follows (experiment: choose mapping per-experiment):
  - Score >= 0.75 -> rel=3 (highly relevant)
  - 0.5 <= Score < 0.75 -> rel=2 (relevant)
  - 0.25 <= Score < 0.5 -> rel=1 (marginal)
  - Score < 0.25 -> rel=0 (not relevant)
- Rationale: preserves ordinal structure and yields sparse high gains for strong winners. We record both raw BT scores and bucketed rels in the manifest for reproducibility.

NDCG calculation details:
- Use NDCG@10 and NDCG@5 as primary metrics. Discount function: log base 2 (standard) with DCG = sum((2^rel - 1) / log2(1 + rank)).
- For each model variant we compute per-query DCG and IDCG (computed from the aggregated reference relevance sequence). Queries with all-zero relevance in the reference are removed from mean metric computations but tracked as a separate "no-signal" slice.
- Normalization: report mean NDCG, median NDCG, and per-query distribution percentiles (p10/p25/p50/p75/p90).

Uncertainty & regression testing:
- Bootstrap CIs: use query-level bootstrap with 1000 resamples to compute 95% CIs for mean NDCG. We resample queries (not pairs) to preserve within-query correlation.
- Delta computation: compute mean NDCG difference (new_model - baseline) and its bootstrap CI.
- Hypothesis testing: paired permutation test (query-level) as primary p-value because distribution is often non-normal. Complement with Wilcoxon signed-rank for robustness.
- Multiple comparisons: when testing multiple slices, apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control at q=0.05.
- Minimum detectable effect (MDE): pre-compute MDE for target power=0.8 given observed baseline variance. If observed delta < MDE, we mark the regression as "underpowered" and recommend increasing sample or focusing on alternative slices.

Slice definitions (examples we used):
- cold_start_users: queries from accounts with < 7 days of history in logs.
- temporal_drift_weekend_vs_weekday: queries sampled from latest 7 days vs baseline month to detect freshness regressions.
- prompt_perturbation_paraphrase: automated paraphrases of the same seed prompts (synonym swaps, reorder clauses).
- numeric_queries: queries containing numeric comparison or arithmetic.
- entity_dense: queries with >2 named entities recognized by NER pipeline.
- long_form: user prompt length > 120 chars.
- no_signal_queries: reference labels are all zero after aggregation.

Per-slice analysis pipeline:
1) Filter queries for slice, ensure at least N_min=200 queries for stable CI. If < N_min, mark as exploratory.
2) Compute mean NDCG and bootstrap CI.
3) Compute delta against baseline and run permutation test.
4) Report sample size, baseline mean, new mean, delta, p-value, FDR-adjusted p-value, and power estimate.
5) Surface top 10 queries in the slice with largest per-query delta for manual review.

Edge cases and QC heuristics:
- Ties prevalence: if >12% of pairs are labeled as "no preference" for a query set, we flag the query as ambiguous and consider lowering rel granularity (2-level rel).
- Annotator drift: track per-worker agreement on seed pairs over time windows; drop workers with sudden drops (>15% delta) in a 24h window.
- Imbalanced pair graph: if candidate-degree variance > 3x median, resample extra pairs to improve connectivity.
- Safety hits: any candidate receiving safety flag by >1 annotator is automatically assigned rel=0 regardless of BT score; surface for policy review.

Deliverables from this run:
- manifest.csv (rows: query_id, candidate_id, candidate_text, BT_score_raw, rel_bucket, pair_count)
- pairs.csv (rows: query_id, left_id, right_id, winner, worker_id, timestamp)
- per_query_ndcg.csv (rows: query_id, baseline_ndcg10, new_ndcg10, delta_ndcg10, boot_lower, boot_upper)
- slice_report.md (per-slice tables + top failing examples)
- annotator-feedback.csv (free-text comments for edge-case analysis)

Recommendations and next steps:
- Run a short pilot (2k pairs) focusing on prompt_perturbation and numeric_queries to validate mapping thresholds for BT->rel buckets.
- Evaluate alternative aggregation: fit BT globally with query-level fixed effects to borrow strength for low-coverage queries and compare NDCG outcomes.
- Add automated paraphrase difficulty scoring: prioritize harder paraphrases in future rounds to stress test robustness.
- For regression gating: require both (a) mean NDCG delta worse than -0.5 points AND (b) at least one slice with adjusted p < 0.05 before blocking a rollout.

Notes and open questions:
- We observed some candidate types with high BT score variance across repeats; need to inspect if workers are conflating format vs content.
- Should we adopt probability-of-preference as soft gains (use raw BT probabilities) instead of discrete rel buckets for a continuous-NDCG variant? Requires metric tooling changes.
- How to best incorporate function-calling/structured outputs where relevance is multi-dimensional? Proposal: multi-axis scoring and weighted composite rel, but will require separate evaluation harness.

Checklist before labeling launch:
- [ ] finalize instruction examples and hidden tests (Diego)
- [ ] confirm seed/query list and candidate extraction pipeline (Priya)
- [ ] verify crowd platform enrichment: worker prequalification + language filters (Liam)
- [ ] implement BT fallback and bucket mapping in eval-runner (Maya)
- [ ] schedule pilot and post-pilot discussion (team)

Contact: maya.chen@redwood.ai for questions or to request a rerun with alternate rel mappings.

Revision history:
- 2026-02-14: initial draft (sampling + annotator instructions)
- 2026-02-21: added BT aggregation and fallback rules
- 2026-03-10: expanded uncertainty testing and slice gating rules
